findings.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Return value of OptimizedImage.downsize (false on convert/gifsicle failure) is discarded, so a failed downsize (missing binary, corrupt image, disk full) is silently ignored and the loop just retries or exits without knowing the resize ever worked.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — New synchronous downsize path trusts extension-based `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` alone, so any upload merely named like an image (regardless of actual bytes) is unconditionally fed to ImageMagick `convert`/gifsicle via shell backticks at upload time, widening exposure to ImageTragick-style RCE in image-parsing libraries beyond the pre-existing async thumbnail job

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL-download size cap is now a hardcoded `10.megabytes` instead of the admin-configured `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, silently bypassing the operator's configured resource/DoS limit for the `is_api?` URL fetch (pre-existing SSRF-capable fetch)

spec/models/optimized_image_spec.rb:0 — No test verifies that a percentage-based dimension string (e.g. "80%") passed to downsize is correctly forwarded to downsize_instructions and produces valid convert instructions, which is the exact new usage introduced in uploads_controller.rb

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Return value of OptimizedImage.downsize (false on convert/gifsicle failure) is discarded, so a failed downsize (missing binary, corrupt image, disk full) is silently ignored and the loop just retries or exits without knowing the resize ever worked.

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` without checking its return value. In optimized_image.rb, `convert_with` returns `false` when the convert/gifsicle command fails (`$?.exitstatus != 0`), so a failure to downsize is silently ignored; the loop will just retry based solely on `tempfile.size` and may exit after 5 attempts without ever detecting that resizing failed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — New synchronous downsize path trusts extension-based `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` alone, so any upload merely named like an image (regardless of actual bytes) is unconditionally fed to ImageMagick `convert`/gifsicle via shell backticks at upload time, widening exposure to ImageTragick-style RCE in image-parsing libraries beyond the pre-existing async thumbnail job

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new synchronous resize loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that runs before `Upload.create_for(...)` and gates solely on `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` (passing only `filename`, not validated MIME/magic bytes). If that predicate can be satisfied by a crafted name, arbitrary uploaded bytes can be fed into `OptimizedImage.downsize`, which ultimately executes external image tooling via shell backticks in `OptimizedImage.convert_with` (`` `#{instructions.join(" ")} &> /dev/null` ``). This introduces a new pre-validation image-parsing execution path at upload time, increasing exposure to vulnerabilities in the image processing stack compared to the prior behavior shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL-download size cap is now a hardcoded `10.megabytes` instead of the admin-configured `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, silently bypassing the operator's configured resource/DoS limit for the `is_api?` URL fetch (pre-existing SSRF-capable fetch)

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes the URL download cap for the `is_api?` path from the admin-configured `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes` (`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`). The later downsizing loop only runs after the file is already downloaded, so it does not preserve the operator-configured resource limit for the network fetch. This is a real behavior/security-relevant change grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/optimized_image_spec.rb:0 — No test verifies that a percentage-based dimension string (e.g. "80%") passed to downsize is correctly forwarded to downsize_instructions and produces valid convert instructions, which is the exact new usage introduced in uploads_controller.rb

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new call site using a percentage string: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` in `uploads_controller.rb`. It also changes `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` to accept and forward an arbitrary `dimensions` string directly to `downsize_instructions` (no longer always building `"#{w}x#{h}"`). The PR diff contains no corresponding spec changes, so there is no diff-evidence of a test covering this new percentage-based usage path.
